dek: A football focused handicapper from Fairport, New York, selling picks since the early 2000s. He runs his own site, mattfargo.com, and is also sold through Big Al, PickDawgz, WinningCappers and the SportsCapping network. The same annual pass cost $1,299 on his own site and $1,999.95 on a network storefront on the same day. Every record we saw is published by a site that sells him, the sellers' own five year figure is about 52.7% winners, and the guarantees pay in credit or free picks, not cash.

short_answer: Matt Fargo is a real, long running pick seller. A saved copy of mattfargo.com from April 2005 shows him selling an MLB season package for $500 under a Covers Media Group copyright, a CappersPicks blog post from September 2008 called him one of its top handicappers, and on 20 Nov 2026 his plays were on sale on his own site and at least five storefronts. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money is a separate question. Every record we saw, such as "108-69-6 (61.0%) Football YTD," is published by a site that sells the picks. The football total adds up only if college football is 68-48-2 (58.6%); the same pages also print college football as "67-41-2 (62%)." The sellers' own five year figure, 598-536 in NFL and college football regular seasons, is about 52.7% winners, close to the 52.4% needed to break even at -110. PickDawgz showed his last 10 plays at 5 and 5 on 20 Nov, after a 2 and 8 stretch on 16 Nov.

Prices vary a lot by storefront. His own site sold the annual pass for $1,299, the 180 day pass for $799 and the 90 day pass for $599; InfoPlays and Capper Reviews, which check out through SportsCapping, listed $1,999.95, $1,499.95 and $999.95 for passes with the same names. Independent buyer comments are scarce and old: one 2013 forum tally of his free plays was slightly losing, and TheRX lists him among services members may not repost.

guarantee: PickDawgz marks his single plays "Credit Guaranteed": if a package does not profit, "a credit for its full purchase price is automatically issued after picks are graded and verified." Credits "expire 9 months after they are added to your account." It is store credit, not cash.

The SportsCapping network, which handles InfoPlays checkout and runs Capper Reviews, adds free time equal to what you bought if a package loses, gives one free period per purchase, grades on 100 unit intervals, and states: "We do not offer a money back policy like some services do." It also says "There is NO GUARANTEE on seasonal subscriptions."

Big Al's refund policy says "there is a no-refund policy on all purchases" and "There are no performance guarantees for any of the purchased picks or subscription packages." It refunds single picks only for games that are cancelled, postponed more than four days, have a pitcher change, or were bought after the start.

His own site says its network handicappers "guarantee all their picks or the next pick of that sport is free." Its terms of use, effective 12 Jul 2014, call the service "FOR ENTERTAINMENT PURPOSES ONLY" and say no refund is owed if access is ended for a breach. None of these versions covers what a buyer loses on the bets themselves, which is usually far more than the package price.

claims_note: How we checked: we read his own site and five storefronts on 20 Nov 2026 and added up the records they print. Where a total is made of parts, we checked that the parts add to it. We also compared these pages with our 16 Nov reading.

The start year differs by storefront: 2000 on Big Al, 2002 on his own site and PickDawgz, and "14 years" in an older bio. Small numbers drift too: college football appears as 67-41-2, 68-48-2, 69-48-2 and 69-47 on pages read the same day, and the primetime NFL figure has appeared as 19-4-1 and 19-3-1. These may be pages updated at different times, but no page shows the underlying list.
The modest number is the long one. The 598-536 five year total, from the same sales pages, works out to about 52.7% winners, much closer to break even than the 61% year to date headline.

The contest claims name Sports Watch Monitor. Its home page, at a Las Vegas mail suite address, offers "Guaranteed Picks," pick packages and a "Become A Capper" sign up, which suggests it sells the handicappers it ranks. We did not find a results page we could open.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. Matt Fargo does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming Matt Fargo most often were BuzzKill (TheRX newsletters thread), Churchillsprts, 1218Sports, Hottie4Sports. From 25 Oct 2026 to 25 Oct 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a Matt Fargo block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.
Result: 2 plays, 2 won, 0 lost, +1.87 units, a return of +93.5% per unit risked. By sport: too few per sport to split. By month: October 2 won, 0 lost, +1.87 units.

What it means: 2 decided plays is far too few to judge. We list them so readers can see what was posted and how it did; the sample covers only plays others chose to post, not the full card a subscriber receives.
What a buyer can verify independently: very little. We found no full, time stamped log of every Matt Fargo pick with line, odds and release time, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the sellers publish: year to date totals, selected runs and short recent lists. On 20 Nov 2026 PickDawgz listed his last 10 plays, 14 to 19 Nov, as 5 wins and 5 losses, including 1 win and 4 losses on the NFL card of 15 Nov. On 16 Nov the same list showed 2 and 8. WinningCappers showed him 47-30 over the past 30 days in all sports and 31-18 in college football. Each of these is graded by a site that sells the picks.

The only outside tally we found is old: in March 2013 a Sportsbook Review member tracked his free picks over a few weeks at 8 wins and 9 losses, about 2 units down. That is a tiny sample of free plays, not his paid card.

Background: a saved copy of mattfargo.com from 15 Apr 2005 shows him selling NBA, college and MLB packages under a "Copyright 1995-2004 Covers Media Group" footer. CappersPicks featured his weekly college football column in Sept 2008. The current mattfargo.com was registered on 22 Aug 2014, its terms are dated 12 Jul 2014, and it lists picks from a dozen other handicappers through WinningCappers affiliate links. Big Al gives his home as Fairport, New York.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Matt Fargo pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Matt Fargo performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the sellers advertise 61% on football this season but about 52.7% over five years. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Matt Fargo is thin. The largest set of comments sits on a site that says it is part of the network selling his picks, and one of those commenters noted how little forum talk about him exists. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found very little buyer talk about Matt Fargo outside the sites that sell him, across more than twenty years of selling. The main pool is 14 undated comments on Capper Reviews, a network owned site: twelve praise his football, basketball and underdog picks, one says he is good in college football but not the NFL and stopped buying his baseball picks, and one calls him possibly the worst handicapper over his baseball losses. Outside the network, one Sportsbook Review thread from 2013 tracked his free picks as slightly losing, and another member there linked a third party record without comment. TheRX lists him among services and write ups members may not repost, without saying why. Reddit archive searches and our saved copy of ten betting subreddits found no post about him. We found no complaints about billing, refunds or delivery, and no independent long term record either way.

Capper Reviews shows a rating of 3.76 out of 5 from 29 votes and 14 undated comments. Twelve are positive, mentioning NFL, college football, WNBA, NBA and MLB winners and one big Colts win; one says he is worth paying for in college football but not the NFL; one is strongly negative about his underdog heavy baseball picks. One of the positive comments also remarks that they see little talk about him on forums. The page says Matt Fargo sells picks through the SportsCapping network, which Capper Reviews is part of, so this is not independent evidence.

In a Sportsbook Review thread about whether tout records hold up, one member who tracked free picks wrote that Matt Fargo's free plays went 8 and 9 over the same stretch, about 2 units down. Earlier in the thread another member asked for his stats, and a third linked an outside record page in reply without comment. Others argued that paid picks are not worth buying in general. This covers free plays only, over a few weeks.

The TheRX service play thread for 1 Nov 2026, where members repost picks from paid services, lists Matt Fargo among services and write ups members should not post. One member had already reposted his NFL play that day. Nobody commented on his results.
The opening post of the 7 Nov 2026 TheRX thread repeats the do not post list, with Matt Fargo on both the services list and the write ups list. The list does not give a reason.

BoydsBets runs a staff written Matt Fargo review that repeats the sales page records and sends every buy button to sportscapping.com with an affiliate code. It has no buyer comments. We treat it as marketing, not a review.

Reddit archive searches for Matt Fargo in r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting returned no posts about the handicapper (the only matches were about a bank and a TV show), and our saved copy of ten betting subreddits had none. Web searches found no Covers thread, BBB listing, news story, lawsuit or regulator record about him.

conflicts: Capper Reviews, which hosts the star rating and comments, says it is part of the SportsCapping network that sells his packages.

BoydsBets and InfoPlays present themselves as review or info sites but send buyers to sportscapping.com checkout, and the BoydsBets links carry an affiliate code. A site paid per sale has a reason to present the seller well.
His own site lists picks from a dozen other handicappers through WinningCappers links tagged with an affiliate ID, so it earns from other sellers' sales too.
Big Al's site, which sells his picks, is run by another handicapper, Al McMordie. Sports Watch Monitor, the source of his contest placings, also sells picks.
strengths: A named handicapper with a long, traceable history: his own site was selling picks in 2005, and a 2008 CappersPicks post already featured his column.
Prices are published for every package on several sites, from $29.99 single plays up, so a buyer can compare before paying.
Buying on his own site was much cheaper for long passes on 20 Nov 2026: $1,299 a year against $1,999.95 on the network storefronts.
The sellers show recent losing results as well as wins, such as the 2 and 8 run on PickDawgz on 16 Nov.
Short packages on PickDawgz and the SportsCapping network carry written credit or free time terms.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw comes from a site that sells the picks.
Headline records do not add up on the same page (67-41-2 versus 68-48-2 in college football), and the start year and years of experience differ between pages.
The five year total the sellers quote, 598-536, is about 52.7%, barely above break even at -110.
The same named long pass cost 54% to 120% more on the network storefronts than on his own site, and the "under $4 per day" line is wrong at the higher price.
Guarantees pay in credit or free picks, never cash; season passes have no guarantee; Big Al offers no performance guarantee at all.
Contest placings cite a monitor that also sells picks, and the main rating page is owned by the selling network.
checklist: Compare the same package on mattfargo.com, InfoPlays, Big Al and PickDawgz before paying; long passes were far cheaper on his own site.
Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A year to date headline is not a record.
Add up the records on the page. If the parts do not make the total, ask why before you buy.
Count units, not wins. A 61% stretch at the wrong prices can still lose money, and the sellers' own five year figure is 52.7%.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Here every version is credit or more picks.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
faq: He is a real handicapper who has sold picks since the early 2000s, through his own site and well known storefronts with published prices. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because no site shows a full record of every pick, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
What does the Watchdog sample of Matt Fargo show?
We graded 2 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 25 Oct 2026 to 25 Oct 2026: 2 won, 0 lost, +1.87 units at one unit each. That is too few plays to judge.

A football focused handicapper from Fairport, New York, who says he started selling picks in 2000 or 2002. He calls himself a situational, contrarian handicapper, writes long game analysis, and was selling picks on mattfargo.com by 2005. He now sells through his own site and several reseller networks.
How much does Matt Fargo cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 single plays were $29.99 ($30 on Big Al). On his own site passes ran $99.99 for 3 days, $149.99 for 7, $349.99 for 30, $599 for 90, $799 for 180 and $1,299 for a year. The SportsCapping storefronts charged $999.95, $1,499.95 and $1,999.95 for the 90 day, 180 day and annual passes.

No cash refunds. PickDawgz gives store credit when a guaranteed package loses, the SportsCapping network adds free time and says it has no money back policy, and Big Al has a no refund policy with no performance guarantee.
Does Matt Fargo have a verified record?

No. The sales pages show year to date totals like 108-69-6 in football and a five year 598-536 figure, all published by the sellers, and some of the parts do not add up. We found no independent, time stamped log.

You get a long running football handicapper with detailed write ups and, on short packages, credit or free time if you lose. What is unproven is whether he beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays; the sellers' own five year figure is about 52.7%. If you buy, compare prices first.
